ddimer_final.note: The pathway's terminating step (ESC 2019, C41: PE-unlikely + D-dimer below the applicable cutoff excludes PE without imaging; the age-adjusted cutoff is the guideline's class IIa consideration, from ADJUST-PE, C38). The band this result falls in — between the fixed and age-adjusted cutoffs — carried a 3-month venous thromboembolic rate of 0.3% among untreated ADJUST-PE patients (C38). On the board, the assay's negative direction (LR- 0.0732 computed from the C39 pooled pair) takes the embolism posterior from 0.12 to 0.0099, below the workbench's 0.02 rule-out line, at stage 2.

pathway_final.note: ESC 2019 exclusion pathway, walked in full: clinical probability (Wells 0.0, PE-unlikely) -> PERC evaluated with precondition met (positive on age alone; cannot exclude) -> age-adjusted D-dimer negative -> PE EXCLUDED at stage 2. No CTPA is indicated at any stage of the adjudicated pathway. This is the branch case 6 recorded in its sources but never walked; its patient's completed Wells of 6.0 routed her to the scanner instead.

perc_final.note: Count 1 of 8 — the age criterion alone — complete at stage 1. PERC positive: the rule declines to exclude. Its use condition, unmet in case 6, is MET here (documented low gestalt; the workbench's stage-1 embolism weight is 0.12, inside the rule's < 15% envelope), so the refusal is the rule working as designed in the population it was built for: it hands the decision to the D-dimer rather than making it.

wells_final.note: Complete at stage 1 and unchanged thereafter: all six objective items assessed, all zero — no DVT signs, heart rate 84, no immobilisation or surgery, no prior VTE, no haemoptysis, no malignancy. Two-tier: PE unlikely. Three-tier: low (< 2). The excluded judgment item's sensitivity (+3 -> 3.0, still PE-unlikely two-tier) is stated in the block note.

adjudication.diagnosis_label: Musculoskeletal chest-wall pain, costochondritis-class (left third and fourth costochondral junctions), after unaccustomed exertion — with pulmonary embolism excluded on the ESC 2019 pathway (Wells 0.0 PE-unlikely; PERC positive on age alone with its precondition met; D-dimer 560 ug/L FEU below the 620 ug/L age-adjusted cutoff) and no imaging required

evidence_chain.criterion: The examination that names the truth
evidence_chain.role: Palpation of the left third and fourth costochondral junctions reproduces the pain exactly — the consulted costochondritis picture's diagnostic core (C51), carried in the 2021 chest-pain guideline's examination table (C50). No consulted source quantifies a likelihood ratio for it, so it moves no board; like case 5's dorsal-branch finding, its force is anatomical and conjunctive, and the case says so rather than inventing a weight.
Unaccustomed heavy upper-body exertion the day before onset — the overuse antecedent the consulted review names (C51). Case data, argued as part of the conjunction.

evidence_chain.criterion: The swelling that is not there
evidence_chain.role: The examined absence that keeps the presentation costochondritis-class rather than Tietze (C51), and the factual ground of the truth's recorded Mondo refusal: the only Mondo class the search returned is defined by the swelling this patient lacks.

One of the six assessed zeros that complete the Wells score at 0.0 at stage 1 — recorded here because in case 6 this same examination, positive, was worth +3 and the whole pathway. A pathway is only as good as its examined absences.

560 ug/L FEU: above the fixed cutoff, below the age-adjusted 620 — the result the whole case turns on. Weighed on the board at LR- 0.0732 (computed, C39) and read on the pathway as the ESC exclusion step (C41, C38).

evidence_chain.criterion: The safety net, run and negative
evidence_chain.role: With the normal ECG: the coronary conjunction. The net exists because reproducible tenderness does not close the coronary question (C51: coronary disease in 3 to 6 percent of such presentations; C50's caution to the same effect), and its negative return is part of why discharge is the disposition.

Ordered a stage after the exclusion, under social pressure; negative, as the pathway predicted. It is in the evidence chain as the attempt's scored error, not as evidence: the exclusion precedes it and does not rest on it.

The 7 mm incidental nodule and the Fleischner surveillance it obliges (C48) — the concrete price of the stage-3 order, of the kind the over-testing cohort quantifies (C49: incidental findings requiring follow-up in 24% of CTPAs).

excluded.basis: Excluded by the walked pathway, not by impression: Wells 0.0 complete at stage 1 (PE-unlikely, two-tier); PERC evaluated with its < 15% precondition met and positive on the age criterion alone, so the rule itself declines and hands over; D-dimer 560 below the age-adjusted cutoff 620 (ADJUST-PE band 3-month failure rate 0.3%, C38) — the ESC 2019 exclusion step (C41). On the board the same step is LR- 0.0732 (C39): posterior 0.0099, below the rule-out line, at stage 2. The stage-4 CTPA's negative result is consistent with the exclusion and is not part of its basis.

Excluded by conjunction, stated rather than weighed: pain fully reproducible on palpation and pleuritic/positional in character (features the 2021 guideline reads against ischaemia, C50), a normal ECG, and a troponin of 6 ng/L below the 14 ng/L threshold (C41) — the declared safety-net pair returning negative. No likelihood ratio is attached to any leg: the consulted sources quantify none for this conjunction, and the case does not invent one. The residual the sources themselves name (C51: coronary disease in 3 to 6 percent of chest-pain-with-tenderness presentations) is exactly what the disposition's safety-netting addresses.

Excluded by conjunction: afebrile (36.8 C), no cough at any point, respiratory rate 16 with SpO2 98% on air, chest clear in all fields, and the declared safety-net panel normal (WBC 6.8, CRP 4). No CURB-65 block is declared: the score grades a pneumonia's severity, and grading an excluded diagnosis would be decoration — the case-6 discipline, applied in reverse.

Excluded by conjunction: symmetric expansion and breath sounds with no absent or reduced air entry, respiratory rate 16, SpO2 98% on room air, and a pain that is palpation-reproducible at the costochondral junctions rather than pleural. No imaging was performed in the adjudicated pathway and none is claimed in its basis.

adjudication.note: The adjudicated diagnosis is a clinical conjunction (reproducible costochondral tenderness + mechanical precipitant + absent swelling, C51/C50) reached AFTER the dangerous hypotheses are excluded by their own instruments — the embolism by its walked pathway, the coronary hypothesis by its declared safety net, pneumonia and pneumothorax by stated conjunctions. That order is the case's thesis: the benign diagnosis is what remains when the pathway has been walked, not a first impression the pathway is then bent to fit.

available_tests.name: 12-lead electrocardiogram
available_tests.note: The ACS safety net's first member, classified safety-net by the machinery: it moves no board, settles no criteria atom, and exists so the must-not-miss coronary hypothesis is tested, not assumed away — the consulted costochondritis review's 3-to-6-percent coronary figure (C51) is the reason the net runs in a presentation whose pain is fully reproducible.

available_tests.name: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin
available_tests.note: The safety net's second member, and in THIS case the machinery agrees with the declaration: no severity block exists for its value to settle (contrast case 6, where the same order landed criteria-completing via the ESC block), so it classifies safety-net. A normal troponin with a normal ECG is the adjudication's coronary conjunction; neither carries a likelihood ratio and none is invented.

available_tests.name: D-dimer (quantitative, FEU)
available_tests.note: Classified discriminating: its negative-direction weight (LR- 0.0732 computed, C39) carries pulmonary embolism across the workbench's rule-out line at stage 2 (0.12 -> 0.0099). Procedurally it is also simply the pathway's next step: PERC could not exclude (positive on the age criterion alone, precondition met), Wells is PE-unlikely, and the ESC algorithm sends exactly this patient to D-dimer (C41). A D-dimer ordered in a PERC-NEGATIVE patient would have been the mirror error — testing past a rule that had already excluded; that error is not available in this case, because this patient's PERC is positive, and the case records the distinction.

available_tests.name: Full blood count and C-reactive protein
available_tests.note: Declared and classified safety-net for the pneumonia hypothesis: the infection screen whose normal values, with the absent fever and cough and the clear chest, form the adjudication's exclusion conjunction. It settles no score atom — CURB-65 is not declared in this case, because the pneumonia it would grade is excluded on the conjunction, and a severity score for an excluded diagnosis would be decoration.

available_tests.name: CT pulmonary angiography
available_tests.note: On the menu from stage 1 — availability is not indication. In the adjudicated pathway it is never ordered: the ESC pathway terminated at stage 2. The model learner orders it at stage 3, under social pressure and after the exclusion, and the machinery classifies it non-contributory: its findings carry no likelihood ratio, settle no criteria atom, and were declared no safety net. Its costs are the consulted ones (C49): a median 10 mSv of radiation, iodinated contrast, and — in this patient — the incidental-finding cascade the cohort quantifies at 24% of CTPAs: a 7 mm nodule and the Fleischner surveillance it now obliges (C48). The module's scored over-testing error, classified by the same machinery that classified every prior case's missed-diagnosis errors.

The seventh item — 'PE is the #1 diagnosis, or equally likely' (+3) — is excluded on case 6's stated grounds (a self-contained case cannot score a clinician-judgment item without circularity), and the sensitivity is shown: with it, the total would be 3.0 — still PE-unlikely on the two-tier reading (<= 4) the ESC pathway uses, so the pathway is unchanged; on the original three-tier bands it would read moderate (2-6) rather than low (< 2), and the case records that difference rather than hiding it. Case 6's Wells completed at 6.0 and sent its patient to the scanner; this score, complete at 0.0, is the first of the three instruments that route this patient away from it.

criteria_blocks.label: PERC — pulmonary embolism rule-out criteria
criteria_blocks.note: The eight PERC criteria (C37), scored as the count of criteria PRESENT: PERC-negative requires all eight absent. Two facts are stated as plainly as the arithmetic. (1) THE PRECONDITION IS MET — the deliberate contrast with case 6: PERC was derived and validated only for patients a clinician has already judged low pretest probability (gestalt < 15%), and this patient meets it — the workbench's own stage-1 embolism weight is 0.12, inside the rule's envelope, on a completed Wells of 0.0. The rule therefore SPEAKS here, as it never could for case 6's post-operative, tachycardic, hypoxaemic patient. (2) SPEAKING, IT DECLINES TO EXCLUDE: the count is 1 — the age criterion alone (62 >= 50); all seven clinical criteria are assessed absent at stage 1, so the block is complete from the first stage. A single birthday is the whole of this patient's PERC positivity, and the pathway's next instrument — the D-dimer, at its age-adjusted cutoff — is the one that decides. PERC's prospective false-negative rate among very-low-risk PERC-negative patients was 0.9% (C37); that figure belongs to patients the rule excludes, and this is not one of them.

findings.text: Age 62 years (case data). Carried as a finding so the age items of the PERC block and the ADJUST-PE cutoff arithmetic evaluate from a measured atom, as case 6's age finding does. The age is load-bearing twice in this case: it is the PERC block's only positive criterion, and it sets the D-dimer cutoff (62 x 10 = 620 ug/L) the pathway turns on.

Left parasternal chest pain, sharp and precisely localised to the left third and fourth costochondral junctions, present for two days, worse on deep inspiration, on coughing and on twisting the trunk; no radiation to arm, jaw or back, no diaphoresis, no exertional pattern (case data).

Onset the evening after a weekend of gardening and moving boxes in a house move — unaccustomed heavy upper-body exertion in the 24 hours before the pain began (case data). The consulted review names physical strain and overuse among the condition's recognised antecedents (C51).

Palpation of the left third and fourth costochondral junctions reproduces the patient's pain exactly — the same quality, at the same site, on every palpation (case data). The finding is the consulted costochondritis picture's diagnostic core: pain reproduced by palpation of the affected cartilage segments (C51), and the 2021 chest-pain guideline's examination table assigns costochondral-joint tenderness to costochondritis and lists palpation with pain reproducibility among the musculoskeletal findings (C50). It carries no likelihood ratio: no consulted source quantifies one for it against this differential, and the case does not invent one — its force is the conjunction it forms with the pathway, argued in the adjudication.

No swelling, heat or erythema over the tender junctions (case data) — an examined absence with a specific job: visible enlargement of the costochondral junction is Tietze syndrome's distinguishing feature on the consulted review (C51), and its absence is what keeps this presentation in the costochondritis class and out of the one Mondo class the ontology search returned (see the truth hypothesis's mondo_note).

Slight breathlessness, attributed by the patient to the pain catching at the top of a deep breath; she is comfortable at rest, speaks in full sentences, and walks the corridor without dyspnoea (case data).
Heart rate 84/min, regular (case data). Below both the Wells (> 100) and PERC (>= 100) thresholds — assessed zeros in both blocks.
Respiratory rate 16/min (case data).
Blood pressure 128/78 mmHg (case data).
Oxygen saturation 98% on room air (case data). Above the PERC block's < 95% criterion — an assessed zero.
Temperature 36.8 C — afebrile (case data). A recorded absence against the pneumonia hypothesis.
No cough at any point in the two days (case data) — a recorded absence against the pneumonia hypothesis.
No haemoptysis (case data). Read by both the Wells block (haemoptysis item) and the PERC block (haemoptysis criterion) as an assessed zero.
No previous objectively diagnosed DVT or PE (case data). Read by both blocks as an assessed zero.
No exogenous oestrogen use (case data). A PERC criterion, assessed absent.

No surgery, no trauma requiring hospitalisation, and no immobilisation in the previous four weeks (case data). Read by the Wells immobilisation/surgery item and the PERC surgery/trauma criterion as assessed zeros — the deliberate mirror of case 6, where the corresponding finding, present, scored in both.
No malignancy, active or under treatment within six months, and none palliative (case data). A Wells item, assessed zero.

Calves symmetric on inspection and measurement, no unilateral swelling, no pain on deep-vein palpation (case data). Read by the Wells DVT-signs item (+3 when present) and the PERC unilateral-leg-swelling criterion as assessed zeros — in case 6 this examination, positive on the un-operated side, was the case's pivotal datum; here its recorded absence is one of the zeros the pathway stands on.

Chest examination: symmetric expansion and breath sounds, all fields clear — no crackles, no wheeze, no absent or reduced air entry (case data). The pneumothorax and pneumonia exclusions in the adjudication read this finding with the vitals.
Light ex-smoker: stopped 22 years ago after roughly five pack-years; no chronic cardiopulmonary disease (case data). Recorded for the incidental-nodule risk reading at stage 4 (C48).

12-lead ECG: normal sinus rhythm at 84/min, no ST-segment or T-wave change, no conduction abnormality (case data). The first member of the declared ACS safety-net pair; it carries no likelihood ratio — its work is exclusion in the adjudication's conjunction, and the machinery classifies the order safety-net.

High-sensitivity troponin 6 ng/L (lab.troponin): below the 14 ng/L threshold the consulted ESC summary uses (C41). The second member of the ACS safety-net pair. Unlike case 6 — where an elevated troponin fed the ESC severity block and the order landed criteria-completing — no severity block exists in this case for the value to settle, and the machinery classifies this order safety-net, as declared. The contrast is the lesson: an order's classification is its mechanical effect in THIS case, not its intent.

lr.note: LR- 0.0732, computed from the consulted pooled pair (C39, Patel et al. 2020, 61 studies): sensitivity 0.97, specificity 0.41. (1 - 0.97) / 0.41 = 0.03 / 0.41 = 0.0732. Case 6 registered this assay's positive direction only and deliberately no negative direction, because its post-surgical patient could never be excluded by it; this patient is the population the negative direction exists for — PE-unlikely on a completed Wells score — and here the negative direction is the pathway's operative step, so it is registered, from the same consulted pair, with the derivation in cases/parameters.json. The board weight is a teaching instrument; the exclusion itself is the ESC pathway's (PE-unlikely + below-cutoff D-dimer), and the ADJUST-PE band this result falls in carried a 0.3% 3-month thromboembolic rate among untreated patients (C38).

findings.text: D-dimer 560 ug/L FEU (lab.d-dimer): ABOVE the fixed 500 ug/L cutoff and BELOW the age-adjusted cutoff for this patient — 62 x 10 = 620 ug/L for patients older than 50 (ADJUST-PE, C38). The margin is 60 ug/L under the age-adjusted cutoff and 60 ug/L over the fixed one: on the fixed reading the pathway continues to imaging; on the age-adjusted reading the ESC 2019 pathway (C41) terminates here — PE excluded, no CTPA. The age-adjusted cutoff is therefore not a refinement in this case; it is the decision.

Full blood count and CRP: white cell count 6.8 x10^9/L (reference 4.5-11.0, C7) and CRP 4 mg/L (reference below 10, C45) — no inflammatory signal (case data). The panel is the pneumonia hypothesis's declared safety net: the exclusion in the adjudication reads these values with the absent fever, the absent cough and the clear chest examination.

CT pulmonary angiography (ordered at stage 3, reported at stage 4): no filling defect in the main, lobar or segmental pulmonary arteries (case data). The result confirms the exclusion the pathway had already made at stage 2 and changes no board weight: it carries no likelihood ratio, because the case registers no negative-direction weight for a test the pathway never required — the PIOPED II pair in the register (C40) was weighed by case 6 in its positive direction, and this case does not manufacture a second direction for a scan whose diagnostic work was already done. The machinery classifies the order non-contributory, and that classification is the scored error.

The same CTPA reports an incidental finding: a single solid pulmonary nodule, 7 mm, in the right upper lobe — a lobe the shipped imaging series do segment (see imaging_assessment), though no nodule is or could be a label in them (case data). The finding is the over-testing cascade made concrete: it obliges surveillance the patient did not have when she walked in — for a single solid 6-8 mm nodule the Fleischner Society 2017 recommendations (C48) are CT at 6-12 months, with a further CT at 18-24 months to consider at her risk reading — arranged in the disposition's follow-up letter. The consulted over-testing cohort (C49) found incidental findings requiring diagnostic follow-up in 24% of CTPAs; this patient is now one of them.

The stage-4 CTPA — not part of the adjudicated pathway — showed no embolus and an incidental 7 mm solid right-upper-lobe nodule now under Fleischner surveillance.

hypotheses.mondo_note: No Mondo class is asserted, on a recorded refusal: an OLS search for 'costochondritis' at Milestone 54 returned exactly one Mondo class — Tietze syndrome MONDO:0001858, which carries 'Costochondritis' among its exact synonyms but whose returned definition specifies idiopathic painful nonsuppurative SWELLINGS of one or more costal cartilages. Swelling is the Tietze picture, and the consulted clinical source (C51) distinguishes costochondritis from Tietze syndrome on exactly that point: costochondritis lacks swelling or induration, and this patient's tender junctions show none (f.costochondral-swelling, an examined absence). A search for 'chest wall pain' returned no chest-wall class. The nearest class Mondo carries therefore describes a condition this patient does not have, and it is not used — the case-2 discipline (MONDO:0001710 declined on the same grounds), recorded in the C10 Milestone 54 addendum.

What neither the atlas's geometry nor the imaging's labels carry is the costal cartilage itself as a labelled structure, which is the honest shape of this module's coverage for a cartilage diagnosis, stated rather than smoothed.
imaging_assessment.statement: Imaging was correctly NOT performed in the adjudicated pathway, and the one scan the attempt contains is the scored error. Two recorded facts bound what the shipped series could have decided in any case, both re-verified by the checker at every run: (1) THE PE QUESTION — the TotalSegmentator v1.0 label set is identical for the two shipped subjects (104 labels each) and contains NO embolus or filling-defect label (asserted for both subjects at Milestone 48 and re-verified here); both series are unenhanced thorax-abdomen-pelvis segmentation datasets, not CT pulmonary angiograms, so no series in this module can show or exclude an embolus — the case-6 honesty block's boundary, unchanged. (2) THE NODULE AND THE CHEST WALL — the same label sets contain NO pulmonary nodule label, so the stage-4 scan's incidental finding is not a label either; and they contain no costochondral or cartilage label, though the ribs themselves ARE segmented (rib_left_3 and rib_left_4 among the 24 rib labels) and the lungs are in the field (five lobes, both subjects) — the anatomy adjacent to both of this case's findings is present in the series, and neither finding is. The stage-4 CTPA is an authored encounter (case data), exactly as every case's decisive imaging in this module is; no imaging_link is declared.

management.alternatives_considered: Three alternatives are recorded so the disposition is a decision, not a default. (1) CTPA at stage 2, before the D-dimer returned — the demand's earlier form: refused on the pathway; imaging a PE-unlikely patient ahead of the assay inverts the ESC order (C41), and the scan's own costs are consulted, not rhetorical (C49). (2) Admission for observation after the exclusion: refused — excluded embolism, a negative coronary safety net, normal vitals throughout, and a benign adjudicated cause make it the same over-testing error in a bed instead of a scanner. (3) Omitting the D-dimer because PERC was 'nearly negative': refused and recorded, because it misreads the rule — PERC positive on any criterion, age included, cannot exclude (C37), and the assay at its age-adjusted cutoff is precisely the instrument the pathway gives this patient. The D-dimer order was not the error; the scan was.
management.disposition: Pulmonary embolism excluded on the pathway at stage 2; musculoskeletal chest-wall pain (costochondritis-class) as the adjudicated cause. Discharge home the same day with: (1) safety-netting stated in the record — return immediately for worsening or new breathlessness at rest, pleuritic pain with fever, coughing blood, a swollen or painful leg, collapse, or pain that changes character (central, crushing, radiating); the safety net exists because the sources themselves price the residual (C51's 3 to 6 percent coronary figure; the ADJUST-PE band's 0.3% 3-month rate, C38) and the case does not pretend the pathway makes return precautions unnecessary; (2) the consulted costochondritis management (C51): analgesia — acetaminophen or an anti-inflammatory where safe and appropriate — avoidance of the activities that produced the chest-wall overuse, and reassurance that the condition is usually self-limited and benign; (3) a follow-up letter carrying the one obligation the stage-3 scan created: Fleischner 2017 surveillance of the incidental 7 mm solid nodule (C48) — CT at 6-12 months, with a further CT at 18-24 months to consider. The workbench adjudicates the pathway and the disposition — the questions this case was built to ask.

physiology_link.gap_statement: Design/07 specifies that the patient IS an engine state. That specification is met here only at the baseline, as in cases 1 and 3: the engine models cardiovascular compensation and (since Milestone 47) a respiratory module, and it has NO chest-wall, musculoskeletal or thromboembolic state — there is no engine state for costochondritis, and none for the embolism this case excludes, and this case does not pretend otherwise. The presentation's authored vitals (heart rate 84, SpO2 98%) are case data, flagged as such on their findings; the engine's resting heart rate is 63.3/min. No respiratory readout is recorded in this link: Milestone 54 was built in parallel with Milestone 53's rebuilding of the respiratory surface, and this case's pathway — scores and an assay, not a blood gas — asserts nothing from that surface. The link is the pinned circulation baseline, identically to case 1's, and that identity is what the checker asserts.
physiology_link.verification: Recorded by data-identity with case 1's physiology link (same command, same trace hash 0x6369b10e9a71c872, same seven baseline outputs), NOT by an engine re-run at Milestone 54: the physiology tree was under parallel construction at Milestone 53 while this case was authored, and profile_case7 asserts the identity of the recorded values with case 1's link rather than re-running an engine whose surface was mid-edit. The resting baseline itself was constructed at Milestones 51-53 to be exactly undisturbed by the respiratory work (zero-at-rest construction), which is what makes the identity claim the right check here.

presentation_stages.narrative: A 62-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with two days of left parasternal chest pain. The pain is sharp, precisely localised to the left third and fourth costochondral junctions, worse on deep inspiration and on twisting, and began the evening after a weekend spent gardening and moving boxes. Pressing on the junctions reproduces her pain exactly. She reports slight breathlessness, which she attributes to the pain catching when she breathes deeply; she is comfortable at rest. Vitals (case data): temperature 36.8 C, heart rate 84/min, blood pressure 128/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 16/min, SpO2 98% on room air. Examination: calves symmetric with no swelling and no deep-vein tenderness; chest clear in all fields with symmetric breath sounds; no swelling, heat or erythema over the tender junctions. The learner must commit a stage-1 board before any result exists.
presentation_stages.title: History, vitals, examination

presentation_stages.narrative: First results return together. ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no ischaemic change. High-sensitivity troponin 6 ng/L — below the 14 ng/L threshold. White cell count 6.8, CRP 4 — no inflammatory signal. And the D-dimer: 560 ug/L FEU — above the fixed 500 cutoff, and BELOW the age-adjusted cutoff for a 62-year-old (62 x 10 = 620 ug/L, ADJUST-PE). On the ESC 2019 pathway this patient — Wells 0.0, PE-unlikely, PERC evaluated with its precondition met — has pulmonary embolism excluded without imaging, and the adjudicated pathway ends here. The learner re-ranks.
presentation_stages.title: First results: ECG, troponin, D-dimer, bloods

presentation_stages.narrative: Before discharge is arranged, the patient's husband asks to speak to the team. His brother died suddenly the previous year; the family was told it was 'a clot'. He asks — firmly, and in her hearing — why no scan has been done: 'Just do the scan, to be safe.' The covering colleague, passing, agrees it would 'put everyone's mind at rest'. No new clinical finding of any kind is recorded at this stage. The learner re-ranks under the pressure, and orders.
presentation_stages.title: The demand

presentation_stages.narrative: CT pulmonary angiography, performed the same evening: no filling defect anywhere in the pulmonary arterial tree — and an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe, a finding that now carries its own surveillance obligation. The disposition is written from the pathway, not from the scan: PE was excluded at stage 2, and the discharge, the safety-netting and the nodule follow-up letter are the stage-4 record. The debrief (generated by tools/case_run.py, independently recomputed by tools/case_check.py) scores the attempt's boards against this adjudication.
presentation_stages.title: The scan returns; adjudication and disposition

review.note: Design/07's verification gates require a review block (>= 2 reviewers) before a case counts as library content, and design/10 applies the same dual-source + reviewer discipline project-wide. No reviewers exist for this project. The gate is recorded UNMET with an empty reviewer list, exactly as Milestones 17, 20, 29, 41, 43 and 48 recorded it; the case's content status stays dual-sourced-draft and its scores formative-only. Nothing in this file fills the gate in on paper.
review.status: UNMET — no named independent expert reviewers exist for this project

case.synthetic_note: SYNTHETIC CASE. The patient is an authored fiction built for teaching; no real patient data exists in this module (design/07, master plan section 8 rule 9: education-only scope). Clinical facts the case uses — the Wells and PERC instruments, the ADJUST-PE age-adjusted D-dimer cutoff, the ESC 2019 exclusion pathway, every likelihood ratio, reference range and cutoff — trace to the sources registered in cases/parameters.json (C35-C51, consulted in-session at Milestones 48 and 54), and the patient's particulars are case data, labelled as such wherever they appear.
case.title: Chest pain and the demanded scan — the pathway that excluded the embolism

validity.consequences: Scores are formative feedback only; no credentialing, progression, or clinical decision may rest on them.
validity.internal_structure: Component scores derived from the case model by stated rules (cases/parameters.json); no composite score is computed, because design/07 defines components (Brier-style calibration, anchoring, evidence quality) and no weights — inventing weights would violate the precision law. Calibration proper needs a case series; seven cases now exist and are still not a calibration series — the debrief says so.
